whoTheyAre.summary: The live source identifies Hararghe Oromo in Ethiopia and ties the record to Oromo, Eastern (hae). Glottolog and a University of Oslo dialect study independently connect Hararge/eastern Oromo speech to the Eastern Oromo code, while Hararghe-specific cultural research documents mirriiysa as one locally studied performance tradition.

religionAndCommunity.summary: PeopleGroups.org supplies an aggregate 'Islam - Sunni' label for this record. It is retained as provider context and is not generalized into a statement about every Hararghe Oromo person's belief or practice.

profile.whyUnreachedIntro: The mission classification is explained only from PeopleGroups.org source-native fields. Oromo dialect identity, Hararghe cultural performance and Sunni identity are not treated as causes of unreached status.

whyUnreached.heading: Current source mission status
whyUnreached.summary: The structured source reports GSEC 1 and less than 2% evangelical presence with no recent church-planting activity; it separately reports Unengaged status and that congregations exist.

whyUnreached.heading: Reported resources remain narrow evidence
whyUnreached.summary: The live record reports Bible and Jesus Film availability. Those fields do not establish distribution, comprehension or use across Hararghe Oromo communities.

claims.text: The live PeopleGroups.org record PG046420 reports PEID 46420, display name Hararghe Oromo, country Ethiopia and primary language Oromo, Eastern (hae).
Glottolog identifies Eastern Oromo with glottocode east2652 and ISO 639-3 code hae and lists Ethiopia as its country.
Glottolog and Janko's dialect-classification dissertation associate Barentu/eastern/Hararge Oromo speech with Eastern Oromo (hae), including documented Hararge-area localities.
claims.interpretationNote: This is linguistic classification evidence and is not used to define a single cultural, political or personal identity for every Hararghe Oromo speaker.

claims.text: A Hararghe Oromo study documents mirriiysa as a socio-cultural performance in which listening, understanding and response are interpreted in socially meaningful interactive contexts.
claims.interpretationNote: The study analyzes a set of performance texts and participating folk performers; it is not generalized into a claim that every Hararghe Oromo person practices or interprets mirriiysa identically.

claims.text: The live PeopleGroups.org record reports 'Islam - Sunni' as the aggregate primary-religion label for PG046420.
claims.interpretationNote: This is a provider classification for one people-group-in-country record, not a statement about every Hararghe Oromo person's belief or practice.

claims.text: The live PeopleGroups.org record reports GSEC 1, less than 2% evangelical presence and no recent church-planting activity for PG046420; it separately reports Unengaged status and existing congregations.
claims.interpretationNote: These source-native fields are retained separately; the candidate does not infer a contradiction-free narrative or make a judgment about individuals.
